rules.source: Dulux Trade Paint Expert (duluxtradepaintexpert.co.uk), product coverage pages; Dulux Trade Vinyl Matt technical data sheet
rules.note: Dulux's own stated coverage varies by product line: standard trade matt/vinyl matt lines are commonly quoted at up to 12-13 m2/litre, while Dulux Trade Vinyl Matt's technical data sheet states up to 17 m2/litre (one coat, on a sound, previously painted surface). There is no single figure true across the brand; the figure printed on the specific tin or technical data sheet governs.

rules.measure: recommended coats for a full repaint
rules.source: Dulux UK, 'How Much Paint Do I Need?' (dulux.co.uk/en/expert-help/how-much-paint-do-you-need)
rules.note: Dulux states two coats for its EasyCare range on bare or significantly different-coloured walls; its one-coat 'Simply Refresh' line is the stated exception, needing only one coat over a similar existing colour.

rules.value: sum each wall's (height x width), then subtract door and window areas calculated the same way
rules.source: Dulux UK, 'How Much Paint Do I Need?' (dulux.co.uk/en/expert-help/how-much-paint-do-you-need)
rules.note: Dulux UK's published method is per-wall (height x width) summed, minus openings, rather than a single perimeter x height shortcut. Litres needed = total paintable area / coverage rate per litre (as stated on the specific tin), x number of coats.

rules.value: 2 x (length + width) x height, minus ~21 sq ft per door and ~15 sq ft per window
rules.source: Aggregated DIY paint-calculator sites (e.g. calcshed.com, turn2engineering.com) rather than a UK paint maker; imperial units as published
rules.note: This perimeter-based shortcut is the common generic DIY-calculator form, not a figure published by Dulux, Crown or another UK/IE paint maker by name; included because the brief asked for 'a paint calculator method (perimeter x height)' and no UK/IE brand's own calculator was found using exactly that shortcut — Dulux's own method (above) is the wall-by-wall one.

rules.measure: time for a DIY decorator to paint a small-to-medium room, including prep and clean-up
rules.note: Checkatrade's published estimate for a small-to-medium room, covering preparation and clean-up as well as painting.
Checkatrade's published average day rate for a painter/decorator in the UK.

rules.measure: professional painter/decorator day rate (UK), alternate published range
rules.source: MyBuilder, 'How Much Does a Painter and Decorator Cost?' (mybuilder.com/painting-decorating/price-guides/painter-decorator-cost)
rules.note: MyBuilder's published day-rate range, built from its stated hourly rate of £16-£38 over a full day; MyBuilder separately states £150-£250/day as a round-number average. Checkatrade's £325/day (above) and MyBuilder's figures are both genuinely published but disagree, reflecting the two sites' different survey methods; both are kept rather than reconciled into one invented number.

rules.unit: m2 of wall surface per day
rules.note: MyBuilder's published figure for typical professional decorator output.

rules.measure: professional cost to paint a room, by room size
rules.value: 350 (small, e.g. bathroom); 450 (medium, e.g. bedroom); 1000 (large, e.g. living room)
rules.unit: GBP per room, labour and materials
rules.note: MyBuilder's published per-room cost bands by room type/size.
